clue.text: Crews in race circuit site missing leading article

indicators.note: missing means the article's letters are absent from the circuit's name

parts.note: Le Mans in France hosts the famous 24-hour motor race
le is the French definite article, a common crossword 'article'

explanation.surface: Pit crews at a famous racetrack find a newspaper editorial has gone astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading article' looks like a newspaper editorial; here it is LE, French for 'the', which sits at the front of LE MANS.
explanation.definitionFit: To man a ship or station is to staff it, so the verb crews is a synonym.

clue.text: Writer with 27 endlessly able to produce 9

indicators.note: the writer plus the clipped heroine are able to produce, by rearrangement, the letters of 9 across

parts.note: the answer to 9 across, a diversion

indicators.note: endlessly means the heroine's name loses its final letter

parts.note: the answer to 27 down, the eponymous heroine

explanation.surface: A cross-referenced puzzle: some writer, teamed with a heroine, makes something entertaining.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer plus EMM (EMMA without its last letter, from 'endlessly') rearrange to give AMUSEMENT, signalled by 'able to produce'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Austen, author of Emma and the novel theme of this puzzle, is a celebrated English novelist.

clue.text: Body covering USA revised one set of beliefs

indicators.note: covering means the person wraps around the other letters

parts.note: a person is a human body, as in 'on one's person'

indicators.note: revised means the three letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral I stands for one

explanation.surface: Somebody has rewritten America's single creed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Body' is a person, as in carrying something on your person. The answer is also the title of Austen's last completed novel, fitting the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A persuasion is a religious or political creed, a body of convictions held by a group.

clue.text: Right part of book — right for father of 6 2, for one

parts.note: the recto is the right-hand page of an open book

explanation.surface: A bookish clue: one page of a volume gives the job of a famous novelist's father.
explanation.walkthrough: '6 2' joins the answers to 6 down and 2 down: Jane Austen. Her father George Austen was a country parson.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Austen's father was the parish clergyman at Steventon, an example of a church incumbent.

clue.text: Sculptures or other form of art, say, divided by working group

indicators.note: divided by means the union sits inside, splitting the reshuffled letters
other form of means the letters of the two words are recast in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
TU, a trade union, is a group of workers

explanation.surface: Statues, or perhaps some other art form, as split up by a committee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'other form of' rearranges both 'art' and 'say' into STAARY; 'working group' is a trade union, TU.
explanation.definitionFit: Statuary is a collective noun for statues, the carved or cast figures of sculpture.

clue.text: Romantic heroine, Juliet, with a new energy, Romeo coming into view

parts.note: J in the NATO phonetic alphabet
E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: coming into means the letter enters the word for view

parts.note: to eye something is to view it
R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Juliet, freshly energised, sees Romeo arrive: a romantic heroine indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: Juliet and Romeo, which look like Shakespeare's lovers, are just J and R from the phonetic alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte Brontë's governess is the title figure of a classic love story.

clue.text: Scraping racket in a game

indicators.note: in means the noise is placed inside the other letters

parts.note: brag is a card game similar to poker
a din is a racket, a loud noise

explanation.surface: Someone is scratching away noisily during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: BRAG is a card game, a forerunner of poker.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrading means wearing down a surface by rubbing, which is what scraping does.

clue.text: See 6
Diversion — something necessary to get round European soldiers

indicators.note: to get round means the necessity surrounds the other letters

parts.note: 'a must' is something essential
men are soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: A diversionary tactic: something vital must outflank European troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diversion' has a military ring beside soldiers, but it means entertainment.
explanation.definitionFit: A diversion is a pastime or entertainment, something that amuses.

clue.text: Religious establishment backed vote for protecting bishops

indicators.note: protecting means the reversed vote surrounds the bishops
backed means the vote is written backwards

parts.note: yea is a vote in favour
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, so BB is two of them

explanation.surface: A church body backed a motion shielding its bishops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' reverses the vote to give AEY; 'vote for' is the old parliamentary yea, not a ballot.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbey is a monastery or convent, a community of monks or nuns.

clue.text: Refers to tourist attractions, repeatedly mentioning these locations

indicators.note: mentioning means spoken out loud; repeatedly because both phrases before it share one pronunciation

parts.note: to cite is to refer to

explanation.surface: A guidebook keeps referring to tourist attractions and naming the places.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'Refers to' (CITES) and 'tourist attractions' (SIGHTS) are pronounced like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sites are places or positions, so locations is a plain synonym.

clue.text: For start of book, two things a knight has?

definitions.text: For start of book, two things a knight has?

parts.words: For start of book, two things a knight has?
parts.note: a knight has a title, Sir, and in his youth served as a page; the two together name a book's opening leaf

explanation.surface: A question about the opening of a book and the attributes of a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: A medieval knight began as a page and is addressed by a title, Sir.
explanation.definitionFit: The leaf at the front of a book that gives its name and author is called by this term.

clue.text: Female not just a provider of entertainment

parts.note: unjust means unfair

explanation.surface: A woman is not just someone who entertains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not just' reads as 'not merely' but means unfair.
explanation.definitionFit: A travelling show of rides and stalls exists to give people fun.

clue.text: Stop and return, if led astray

indicators.note: astray means the letters wander out of their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Halt and go back if you have been led off course.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket term: fielders stop the ball and throw it back.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket and baseball, fielders stop a hit ball and send it back in.

clue.text: Like some old people here, having reduced fishing around area

indicators.note: around means the shortened word goes round the letter for area
reduced means the word for fishing loses its last letter

parts.note: angling is fishing with rod and line

explanation.surface: Some old folk round here have cut back on fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' drops the final G of ANGLING; 'around' puts it round A. The Angles were a Germanic people who settled in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglian describes the Angles, ancient settlers of eastern England, so it fits old people of this country.

clue.text: Musical performance originally arranged round old piano

indicators.note: round means the rearranged letters surround the other two
originally means the letters return to some other original order

parts.note: taken as written
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A piece of music first arranged for an old piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' turns ARRANGED into GRANDERA; 'round' puts it around OP. 'arranged' looks like the anagram signal but is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand opera is a large-scale operatic form, sung throughout, a kind of musical performance.

clue.text: PM once linked with partner in 19th-century novel

definitions.meaning: Lord ... was British Prime Minister during the American War of Independence
Elizabeth Gaskell's novel ... and South pairs this compass point with its opposite

explanation.surface: A former prime minister is tied to a partner in a Victorian novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord North led the government 1770-82, and Gaskell's 1855 novel is titled with this point plus South.

clue.text: Final stanza that may be read in broken voice

indicators.note: that may be read in means the letters sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A poem's last verse delivered in a cracking voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken voice' suggests an anagram of VOICE, but the answer is simply sitting in brokEN VOIce.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoi is a short closing stanza of a ballade or similar poem, addressed to someone.

clue.text: The writer is caught by very upset assistant in compromising position

indicators.note: caught by means the writer's words are held within the other letters
upset in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: an aide is an assistant
the writer of the clue says I am

explanation.surface: The setter is caught by a very upset aide in an awkward position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compromising position' suggests scandal but means a halfway point. 'upset' turns AIDE into EDIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Via media is Latin for the middle way, a position between two extremes.

clue.text: Cast lacking confidence in company

definitions.meaning: to throw, as at a coconut ...

explanation.surface: A cast of actors lacking confidence when in company.
explanation.definitionFit: To shy is to fling, and someone shy is timid with other people.

clue.text: Displaying either component of a novel by a lady

definitions.text: Displaying either component of a novel by a lady

parts.words: Displaying either component of a novel by a lady
parts.note: Sense and Sensibility was published as 'By a Lady'; the answer shows sense, and also resembles sensibility

explanation.surface: Describing something that shows part of a novel by an anonymous woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Austen's first published novel was credited only to 'A Lady'.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means showing good sense, and it also echoes the novel's second abstract noun.

clue.text: Head off old car, producing road rage, for example

indicators.note: head off means the first letter of the old car is removed

parts.note: banger is British slang for a battered old car

explanation.surface: Cutting off someone in an old jalopy produces road rage.
explanation.walkthrough: BANGER is British slang for a battered old car. 'Head off' sounds like intercepting someone; it drops the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Road rage is an example of furious temper, an outburst of wrath at the wheel.

clue.text: Portray female author as progressively involved

parts.note: to draw is to portray
Anaïs Nin was a French-American diarist and author

explanation.surface: Depicting a woman writer as becoming steadily more engaged.
explanation.definitionFit: Being drawn in means gradually becoming caught up or engaged in something.

clue.text: Diamonds I'd turned into money, like a rotter

indicators.note: into means the letters go inside the word for money

parts.note: cash is money
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

indicators.note: turned means the two letters run backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cad turns his diamonds into money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses the I'd; 'into' signals insertion. Rotter is old British slang for a scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A cad is a dishonourable man, a rotter, so caddish behaviour is that of a rotter.

clue.text: Author in part of Greece penning article

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as in a pen for animals

parts.note: Crete is a Greek island
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A writer on a Greek island composes an article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Author' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To author something is to originate or make it, a synonym for creating.

clue.text: Stupid people do it after change of heart, interrupting lives

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into the two letters

parts.note: is means exists, lives

indicators.note: change of heart means the central letters of the phrase swap places

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fools do something after changing their minds, disrupting lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after change of heart' swaps the two middle letters of 'do it', giving DIOT; 'lives' means exists.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiots are fools, people who lack sense.

clue.text: Page about fictional hero holding one cold and negative attitude

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: holding means the hero contains the next letters

parts.note: Jude the Obscure is Thomas Hardy's hero
the Roman numeral I stands for one
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A page about a novel's hero who is lonely, cold and negative.
explanation.walkthrough: JUDE is Hardy's Jude the Obscure. The answer recalls Austen's Pride and Prejudice.
explanation.definitionFit: Prejudice is a preconceived and usually unfavourable opinion of someone.

clue.text: Explorer in rescue vessel put under pressure

indicators.note: put under in a down clue means placed below the other letter

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
Noah's ark rescued the animals from the flood

explanation.surface: An explorer in a lifeboat is put under strain.
explanation.walkthrough: Mungo Park was a Scottish explorer of the Niger.
explanation.definitionFit: Mungo Park, the Scottish traveller, charted the Niger river in West Africa.

clue.text: For instance, game briefly written up in press

indicators.note: written up in a down clue means the letters run upwards, backwards

parts.note: eg means for instance
RU is short for rugby union

explanation.surface: A sports report is written up in the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press' looks like the newspapers but is the verb meaning to push for something.
explanation.definitionFit: To press someone is to urge them, to push them to act.

clue.text: Sense of achievement from hunting animals collectively

definitions.meaning: satisfaction in what one has done
the collective noun for a group of lions

explanation.surface: Satisfaction from going out after game.
explanation.definitionFit: Pride is satisfaction in one's achievements, and the collective noun for a group of lions.

clue.text: Eponymous heroine, such as Madame Bovary

definitions.meaning: Austen's novel takes its title from its heroine's first name
Flaubert's adulterous heroine is called by this first name

explanation.surface: A title heroine, the like of Flaubert's Madame Bovary.
explanation.definitionFit: Austen's Emma Woodhouse gives her novel its title, and Flaubert's heroine shares the first name.

clue.text: Demolish east wing of building in a sorry state

parts.note: to ruin is to wreck, demolish

indicators.note: east wing means the right-hand end letter of the word, as east lies right on a map

explanation.surface: Knocking down the east wing leaves the building in a dreadful condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a sorry state' looks like dilapidation but means regretful.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruing means regretting, so someone doing it is feeling sorry.

clue.text: A short sentence added to American volume without changing any characters

indicators.note: added to means the next pieces follow the American volume

parts.note: liter is the American spelling of litre

indicators.note: short means the last letter of the sentence is dropped

parts.note: time is a prison sentence

explanation.surface: A brief jail term is tacked onto a US measure, with the wording untouched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts TIME to TIM. 'characters' means letters, not people.
explanation.definitionFit: Literatim is Latin for letter by letter, an exact copy with no letter altered.
